approach: Follow the partial_release route: keep the authors' ADABORD boosting, aRPS, weight-update, voting, and metric code unchanged, and replace only the missing OGini tree dependency. The port uses the fact that OGini on Q ordinal classes equals, up to a constant factor, multi-output Gini on the Q-1 cumulative binary targets 1(y<=q), so a stock sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier fit on those cumulative targets with sample weights gives exactly the same split criterion and weighted leaf cumulative probabilities. Run a disclosed scaled-down slice (4 small Q>=5 TOC-UCO datasets, 5 splits, 3-fold CV, 3 random-search configs, 50-100 trees) rather than the paper's 31 datasets x 30 splits x 20 configs. The exact 0.823 +/- 0.046 over 31 datasets is out of budget; results/metrics.json will report the subset AMAE and explicitly mark it as a partial reproduction, not an exact match.

files.purpose: Central configuration: dataset list and fallback selector, split counts/seeds, CV/search protocol, estimator candidates, tree/boosting hyperparameters, metric names, output paths, and time-budget guards.

Download/extract the TOC-UCO repository with Python requests+zipfile, parse dataset files and metadata, select four small Q>=5 datasets, load repository 70/30 partitions when present, otherwise generate 5 stratified 70/30 splits with fixed seeds.

Sklearn-compatible OGiniDecisionTreeClassifier: fit stock DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion='gini') on cumulative binary targets with sample weights, convert multi-output leaf probabilities to ordinary class probabilities, expose predict/predict_proba/get_params/set_params. Includes the proof-by-equivalence docstring for OGini.

Import the authors' adabord package, monkeypatch the module-level DecisionTreeClassifier references in adabord._adabord_base and adabord._adabord with OGiniDecisionTreeClassifier, and expose the unchanged ADABORD estimator.
Wrap the authors' adabord._metrics functions; provide exact fallback implementations of AMAE, QWK, MMAE, and BACC using labels mapped to 1..Q; enforce per-split metric computation before averaging.

Cheap same-split baselines: stock sklearn AdaBoostClassifier with standard Gini trees, and XGBoost multi:softprob if installable; used only as sanity comparisons, not to validate the full eight-method ranking.

Run the scaled protocol: for each dataset/split tune n_estimators by 3-fold stratified CV over the scaled candidate set, select by mean AMAE, refit on the full training partition, evaluate ADABORD and baselines on the test partition, aggregate mean/std over executions.

Single entrypoint: prepares data and repo, runs smoke or full scaled experiment, writes results/metrics.json with claim C1 comparison, protocol disclosure, per-dataset/per-split values, and limitations.

config.dataset_selection_rule: 4 smallest TOC-UCO datasets with Q>=5 and N<=2000; exact names verified from Table 1/metadata at runtime (scale-down, route)
config.fallback_dataset_selection: If a named dataset is unavailable, auto-select the first 4 datasets with Q>=5 and N<=2000
config.split_seed_start: 0 (A5 fallback; use repository seeds/partitions if present)
config.criterion: OGini via cumulative multi-output Gini equivalence (R1/R2)
config.sample_weight: used in every base-tree fit (paper Sec 3.2/R3)
config.leaf_probabilities: sample-weight-normalised leaf class frequencies, no smoothing (A2/A9)
config.weight_update: w_i <- w_i * exp(alpha_m * 1(y_i != f_m(x_i))); then renormalise to sum 1 (R9)
config.final_aggregation: weighted hard-label majority vote, argmax_q sum_m alpha_m 1(f_m(x)=q) (R10)
config.arps: mean absolute difference of cumulative probabilities divided by Q-1 (R4/R5/R7)
config.metric_averaging: compute each metric per test split, then mean/std over 5 executions (A14)
config.baseline_adaboost_n_estimators: 50 (scaled; paper base AdaBoost config not fully specified)

steps: Setup: verify Python 3.12 and stock scikit-learn; clone https://github.com/ayrna/adabord if absent; do NOT install the git+ssh scikit-learn fork. Download https://github.com/ayrna/tocuco via requests as zip and extract with zipfile, trying main then master branch.

Inspect the authors' adabord/_adabord.py, adabord/_adabord_base.py, and adabord/_metrics.py to record constructor signatures, where DecisionTreeClassifier is instantiated, whether fit receives sample_weight, and whether predict_proba is expected to return ordinary class probabilities.

Implement ogini_tree.py. In fit(X, y, sample_weight): build Ycum[:,q]=1[y<=q] for q=1..Q-1, fit internal DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion='gini', max_depth=..., random_state=..., min_samples_split=..., min_samples_leaf=...) on Ycum with sample_weight. In predict_proba: read internal multi-output P(Ycum_q=1), set c_Q=1, compute p_1=c_1, p_q=c_q-c_{q-1}, p_Q=1-c_{Q-1}, clip to [0,1] and renormalise. predict returns classes_[argmax(predict_proba)].
Add get_params/set_params so sklearn clone and the authors' code can treat the wrapper like a DTC; accept and ignore criterion='ogini' if passed.

Unit-test the OGini equivalence in ogini_tree.py on a tiny 3-class dataset: enumerate candidate thresholds, compute direct OGini(D)=sum_q c_q(1-c_q) weighted child impurity decrease, and compare the chosen split to the wrapper's internal tree split. Abort if they disagree.

Implement data.py: parse TOC-UCO .train/.test or partition files, use repository-supplied 70/30 partitions if found; otherwise generate 5 stratified 70/30 splits with seeds 0-4. Parse class labels from the last column and map them to 1..Q. Select the four configured Q>=5 datasets or the fallback rule.

Implement metrics_utils.py around adabord._metrics. If the author functions are present and return the expected AMAE/QWK/MMAE/BACC, call them unchanged. Otherwise implement AMAE=mean over classes of MAE, MMAE=max over classes of MAE, QWK with quadratic weights on labels 1..Q, and BACC=mean per-class recall.

Implement adabord_port.py: import adabord._adabord_base and adabord._adabord, replace their module-level DecisionTreeClassifier symbol with OGiniDecisionTreeClassifier, and expose ADABORD. Keep all boosting/aRPS/weight/vote code unchanged.

Run smoke: glass, one stratified split, n_estimators=10, max_depth=3, one config. Fit ADABORD, check predict shape, predict_proba rows sum to 1, alpha and sample weights are finite, and AMAE/QWK/MMAE/BACC are finite. Run standard AdaBoost on the same split as a sanity check.

Run intermediate checks on all selected datasets: N, Q, class counts, 70/30 split sizes, stratification, and that every Q>=5. Check that the wrapper's cumulative probabilities are monotone within each row.

Full scaled run: for each dataset and split, evaluate the 3 sampled configurations from estimator_candidates_scaled using 3-fold stratified CV on the training partition, selecting lowest mean AMAE (tie-break lower STD then fewer estimators). Refit the best config on the full 70% training partition.
Evaluate the refitted ADABORD on the 30% test partition with AMAE, QWK, MMAE, BACC. Repeat for the cheap baselines on the same split. Store per-split and per-dataset values.

Aggregate: compute mean and STD over all dataset/split executions and over datasets. Write results/metrics.json with claim_id C1, reported_value 0.823, tolerance 0.138, measured_subset_mean_AMAE, measured_subset_std, per_dataset, per_split, baseline_means, protocol disclosure, and status 'partially_reproduced' or 'not_reproduced_at_scale' depending on whether the subset mean falls within the tolerance.

Budget guard: before the full loop, time one dataset/split with 50 trees. If projected full time exceeds 14 minutes, automatically reduce to 3 datasets x 3 splits x 50 trees and record the reduction in metrics.json.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: load glass, build one stratified 70/30 split with seed 0, fit OGiniDecisionTreeClassifier on a toy 3-class problem to verify the OGini split equals direct brute-force OGini, then fit ADABORD with n_estimators=10 and max_depth=3 on the real split. Assert predict shape (n_test,), predict_proba shape (n_test,Q), rows sum to 1, cumulative probabilities are monotone, all metrics are finite, and standard sklearn AdaBoost also runs on the same split.
intermediate_checks: TOC-UCO extraction found all four selected datasets and parsed the expected number of rows/features/classes; Q>=5 for every selected dataset.
Class balance per dataset: print counts per class and flag classes with fewer than 3 examples because stratified 3-fold CV and 70/30 splits can fail.
Split integrity: each training partition is 70% and test 30%, every class appears in both partitions where possible, and repository partitions are used when available.
OGini equivalence: on a toy dataset, the wrapper's chosen split threshold matches the threshold that minimises direct weighted OGini impurity decrease; repeat for 2-3 random toy sets.
Leaf probabilities: predict_proba rows sum to 1, are nonnegative, and cumulative sums are nondecreasing; hard labels are in classes_.
Boosting internals: after one ADABORD iteration, err_m is in [1e-10,1-1e-10], alpha_m is finite, updated sample weights sum to 1, and final hard-vote predictions are in classes_.
Parameter/runtime check: one dataset/split with 50 trees completes within a few seconds; count tree nodes and cap min_samples_leaf only if a tree exceeds the memory guard, recording the deviation.
Sanity baseline: standard AdaBoost on glass/one split gives a finite AMAE in the expected 0.8-0.9 range; if not, debug data parsing before the full run.
budget_plan: Setup 4 minutes: clone/verify adabord, download/extract TOC-UCO, parse metadata, implement and unit-test the OGini wrapper. Smoke 2 minutes: one glass split with 10 trees plus the brute-force OGini equivalence check. Full run 14 minutes: 4 datasets x 5 splits x (3 configs x 3 CV folds + 1 final fit) with 50-100 trees, parallelised over dataset/split up to 8 workers; if the timing guard projects over 14 minutes, fall back to 3 datasets x 3 splits x 50 trees and record the scaled protocol in results/metrics.json.
